answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring a refundable deposit for each identity. Every agent locks a deposit of jade before its beacon is admitted to the nebula of registered peers, and each additional identity demands its own separate deposit. Peers can challenge an account at any time, and the deposit is slashed when two identities are proven to share one operator. A sybil attacker who wants N fake identities must lock N deposits, so his cost grows linearly with every fake while an honest agent pays just once. Beyond a few accounts the attack simply stops being profitable.
